title: Lumen - Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Lumen's search stack and evaluate Redwood for embeddings + reranking. Key concerns: integration with existing Elastic/OPensearch, throughput (target 200 qps peak), embedding dimensionality (256 vs 768), hybrid BM25 + ANN architecture, SOC2/KMS requirements, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing options and security docs; SE to propose benchmark plan; Lumen to provide sample corpus and QPS profile.
next_steps: Jordan: Send tailored pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (by 2026-09-02)
Priya: Share benchmark plan + required sample data format (by 2026-09-04)
Evan: Share representative sample corpus and expected QPS distribution (by 2026-09-01)
Schedule technical deep dive + benchmark run (proposed 2026-09-08 09:00 PT)
Share SOC2 report and KMS integration notes
action_items: Jordan Hayes: Send pricing and deployment comparison by 2026-09-02
Priya Rao: Prepare benchmark plan and test harness for throughput/latency by 2026-09-04
Evan Cole: Provide 100k-document sample and QPS histogram by 2026-09-01
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-30 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Lumen), Evan (Lumen), Samir (Lumen)

00:00 - Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm jordan, AE at Redwood. Priya is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:07 - Marta Ruiz: Good thanks, excited to get into this. we put this together because our search relevancy has regressed as we scale embeddings.
00:12 - Samir Desai: yeah thx. high level: we run Elastic for indexing, currently hybrid BM25 + some ANN with vectorstore, but cost and latency are creeping up.
00:22 - Priya Rao: thanks. quick question on scale — what's your peak qps and typical doc size?
00:26 - Evan Cole: peak around 150–200 qps for search, doc text length avg ~600 tokens, we have ~12M documents. currently embeddings are 768-d; looking at 256 to save cost but worried about quality drop.
00:40 - Jordan Hayes: got it. so main constraints are latency, cost, and integration with Elastic — does that capture it?
00:45 - Marta Ruiz: yep, and security — we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS for keys. For some customers, we may need VPC/private options.
00:53 - Priya Rao: great, that maps well to what we do. quick orientation: Redwood offers Hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, and Private for VPC or on-prem. For embeddings/rerank, we support exporting embeddings into vector DBs like Pinecone/Weaviate, or you can run rerank inside our runtime and only store smaller candidate sets back to Elastic.
01:12 - Evan Cole: can you clarify "rerank inside your runtime" — do you mean we send top-k from Elastic to Redwood and you run cross-encoder?
01:18 - Priya Rao: exactly. typical flow: Elastic or BM25 returns top N (say 100), you call Redwood for embedding similarity + rerank, or we do embedding-only recall and let Elastic do the final rank. We also support hybrid pipelines — BM25 + ANN recall, then quick embed similarity for reordering.
01:36 - Samir Desai: what's the throughput for that? 200 qps with rerank seems heavy if you're running cross-encoder.
01:41 - Priya Rao: fair point. for cross-encoder rerank we recommend batching candidates and using our Dedicated option for predictable throughput. On Hosted small scale, we can handle lower qps but latency will be higher. Typical numbers: with Dedicated reserved GPUs you can sustain hundreds of reranks per second depending on model size; with optimized embedding-only rerank we can keep per-request latency low — sub 100ms for vector similarity on ANN index.
02:02 - Jordan Hayes: another lever is embedding dimensionality. moving 768->256 reduces storage and network overhead ~3x, but quality tradeoff depends on your dataset. we can run ablation during the benchmark.
02:15 - Marta Ruiz: our concern is retrieval quality — we can't afford a big hit to relevancy. whats your experience with 256 vs 768?
02:21 - Priya Rao: in many web QA/faq datasets, 256 can be fine if you train/normalize correctly; for nuanced semantic search, 768 or 1024 can help. we usually run offline nDCG on your devset. also quantization and PQ on vector DBs can affect quality; we recommend end-to-end evals.
02:37 - Evan Cole: about Vector DB integration — we currently use Elastic + a lightweight HNSW. would integrating Pinecone be painful?
02:43 - Jordan Hayes: integration is straightforward — we have connectors and SDK snippets. you can either push embeddings from Redwood to Pinecone, or keep embedding generation in Redwood and index in your vector DB. for private deployments we support direct network peering/VPC endpoints to the vector DB.
02:58 - Samir Desai: security: SOC2, SAML, KMS — do you have SOC2, and can keys stay in our KMS?
03:05 - Jordan Hayes: yes SOC2 Type II available. for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration for encryption at rest; Dedicated gives more isolation and Private lets you keep keys entirely on prem depending on setup. we'll share the security whitepaper.
03:19 - Priya Rao: one gotcha: if you want sub-50ms end-to-end rerank with cross-encoder, you'll likely need Dedicated with pinned GPU capacity and optimized batching; otherwise, embedding-only flows or smaller cross-encoders help.
03:32 - Marta Ruiz: what's the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated? and is Dedicated monthly commit-based?
03:36 - Jordan Hayes: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits — tends to be more cost-effective for sustained throughput. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and quicker to start. We'll send a pricing comparison with example QPS scenarios.
03:51 - Evan Cole: on hybrid search: we use BM25 first to surface precise lexical matches, then embed re-rank. does Redwood support rerank-as-a-service where we only send candidate ids and text?
03:59 - Priya Rao: yes, you can send document ids + snippets; our SDK can fetch embeddings from Redwood or compute embeddings on the fly, then rerank. We also support streaming results back for low-latency UX.
04:12 - Samir Desai: what's the expected latency for a 3-stage pipeline: BM25 -> ANN recall -> cross-encoder rerank (top 20)?
04:18 - Priya Rao: rough estimate: BM25 ~20–50ms (on your Elastic), ANN recall ~20–50ms, cross-encoder rerank for top 20 depends on model — small cross-encoder on Dedicated could be ~30–80ms; net end-to-end 80–200ms. again depends on batching and network hops.
04:33 - Marta Ruiz: can we run a benchmark with our traffic pattern?
04:36 - Priya Rao: yes. typical plan: you share a sample corpus and QPS profile, we run two experiments: (1) embedding-only recall + ANN with 256/768 embeddings to compare nDCG and latency; (2) BM25 + top-N rerank with a cross-encoder on Dedicated to measure end-to-end latency. We'll provide scripts and a harness.
04:54 - Jordan Hayes: for integration — if you want to keep Elastic as primary index, we can push small candidate sets back into Elastic or store vectors in Pinecone and have Elastic be the lexical source. Either way we support hybrid.
05:04 - Evan Cole: question on dimensionality again — do you have any internal benchmarks comparing 256 vs 768 on FAQ-like corpora?
05:10 - Priya Rao: we have internal benchmarks and we can run an ablation on your devset; results vary but we frequently see small drops for 256 on nuance-heavy corpora. we'll include nDCG numbers in the report.
05:21 - Marta Ruiz: compliance around logs and audit — we need audit trails of inference for regulated customers, can Redwood provide request logs and redaction controls?
05:29 - Jordan Hayes: yes, Redwood Console provides audit logs per request, RBAC for access, and retention controls. For Private, you can set retention internally. We'll attach the audit log sample and RBAC doc.
05:40 - Samir Desai: network topology: if we do Dedicated vs Private, what's the network layout? we want minimal egress for PHI customers.
05:48 - Priya Rao: Dedicated runs in our managed environment but can be configured with VPC peering, private subnets, and no public egress if required. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control to keep traffic internal and meet stricter data residency.
06:02 - Evan Cole: we'll want to run a throughput test simulating 200 qps with 100 top-N candidates for rerank. is that feasible?
06:09 - Priya Rao: yes, that's basically our benchmark scenario. for 200 qps with cross-encoder rerank on top-100, we'd recommend Dedicated with autoscaling policies and burst capacity. We'll size GPUs and batch sizes in the benchmark.
06:21 - Jordan Hayes: competitors — anything you've tried like Pinecone or Weaviate?
06:24 - Marta Ruiz: tried Pinecone but cost at scale was high; also looked at Weaviate. we care about support and integration with our existing Elastic investment.
06:33 - Priya Rao: understood. our differentiators for you would be unified serving (embeddings + rerank), predictable Dedicated throughput, and VPC/private options for compliance.
06:46 - Samir Desai: any limits on embedding dimension or model sizes? can we bring our own models?
06:50 - Priya Rao: we support common dimensions up to 1024 and custom sizes depending on the model. You can bring your own models for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer curated models and verified performance profiles. For Dedicated we can onboard custom models subject to compatibility checks.
07:05 - Evan Cole: ok cool. timeline: we're hoping for a POC within 3–4 weeks.
07:09 - Jordan Hayes: sounds reasonable. next steps recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, SE will send benchmark plan, and you (Evan) will provide sample corpus & QPS histogram. propose technical deep dive/benchmark on 2026-09-08 09:00 PT.
07:28 - Marta Ruiz: that works, i'll flag internal stakeholders. thanks all.
07:33 - Jordan Hayes: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "rerank" appears as "re-rank" or "re rank"), proper nouns like "Weaviate" sometimes mis-typed, timestamps are approximate.
